title: Lake job, a singer's trick and keeping faith with employers
summary: Joseph describes a Lake concert club job, a woman who tried to take a job from him, and how he gets mostly white engagements.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: That's right, that's right. Now, we got, you know, I got me coming, um, about two Saturdays from now, I'm going over to Lake, at the concert club over there. They said, Louis concert club, I used to go over there before. Well, the man had it, what he's paying for a good price and all, well, like I told the man, he had asked me, could I have more pieces? I told him, he's all right with me. He wants, I used to go over there with six, he wanted to bring eight. So, last time we went, he said, Julie, you better bring your six piece. back. I'm going to tell you what the man told me. Now, listen to me, because y'all people know it. He said, you got two man up there, the man's not playing. Now, I'll show you how man knows, what you doing. I said, what you mean? It's his saxophone over there. That man's not playing. That other saxophone play, he's not playing. Just make one blow, and he takes his own. This man's playing. What he's talking about that, do you understand what I mean? Well, he said, you better bring your little band like this. Now, he hired me to bring the little small band. The man, I knew what they were doing, but the man made me feel so embarrassed. You understand what I mean? I couldn't open my mind. All I had to say, well, yes, you understand what I mean? I knew that. And you see a big band, and you take it, you know you all been around. You see a big band with 10 or 12 pieces. All that guys are going to be playing in that band. There are about six or seven playing in that band. You understand what I mean? It's four man's, it's not doing nothing in that band. We're just expecting the same money, what the other fellas is getting. You understand? Well, and people ain't nobody school anymore. No. People ain't nobody school. See a piano player, he's all the time working. A drum player, a little good drum player, he's got the way. A guitar player, he's got the way. A man playing trumpet, he's got the way. What's he three sides for him? They ain't got the way going. No, they ain't got the way going. A man playing bass, he's got the way. See, he's got to be hornet, and you know he's working. What's he three sides for him? They ain't three, three trumpets, it's one of them trumpets that ain't doing nothing in there. That's right. You set aside, you can see. You can tell the difference. And then got so, I was telling the wisest in town, like I've been running to my little band, with, I'm going to want to many of them fellas. Many fellas say, I try to be hornet, but I'm not no hornet fella. See, when I go, and a man hire me, I'm going to all the time to try to give a man service. I want to come back to a man. I don't want to never go back to the same man. I make me feel pride to go back. What if I go there doing wrong, I'm never going to go back to the man. Am I wrong? See, the man going to say, you done me a little dirty trick. He'll tell me one, he just said, you know where I'll get you no more? You done me a little dirty trick. All right. Tell you what that happened else. I played Espinade and Dolphine from Miss Claiborne Williams. You heard of her? Oh, yeah. She's in the City Hall. Well, she's good friends with the people I work for. Miss Robat, she's living over in St. Louis right now. They call her Claiborne Williams, stayed right there from me and Dolphine in the house upstairs. Big house. They got a whole lot of old colored folks stay with them and dance with red reds. We played the big dance and that for them. Man, them people treat us so fine. and I had, what the only thing made me bad with me, made me, I have to tell you, I had them done a little dirty trick. I had Emily, Emily, Emily, Emily, the sweet, the bell go over, you know what I'm doing? You know what she done me, Bill? It's nothing good.
